story_type: rocket engine full duration hot fire on a test stand
hook: A Moon rocket engine, bolted down and fired for 200 seconds.
narration: This rocket engine roared for three minutes and twenty seconds, bolted to a test stand.
It is an RS-25, the kind that launches NASA's Moon rocket, fired at Stennis Space Center in Mississippi.
This developmental engine will never fly. Its whole job is to be tested.
Every run gives NASA and L3Harris data to make the flight engines perform better and last longer.
Below it, a flame deflector turns the blast sideways, away from the stand.
[short pause] Four of these together make up to two million pounds of thrust.
outcome: It ran the full planned three minutes and twenty seconds, then shut down.
title: Moon rocket engine fired for 200 seconds
description:
NASA tests RS-25 developmental engine No. 10001 for its full planned duration of 200 seconds on the Fred Haise Test Stand at Stennis Space Center, Mississippi, Nov. 18, 2026.

facts.claim: Tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 Nov. 18, 2026 at Stennis
facts.source_quote: tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 on Nov. 18, 2026, on the Fred Haise Test Stand

facts.claim: Developmental engine will not fly; data for L3Harris and NASA
facts.source_quote: While this developmental engine will not be used in flight, the hot fire test provides NASA and NASA’s prime engine contractor L3Harris Technologies with the capability to capture critical data to improve engine performance and reliability

facts.claim: Four engines, up to 2 million pounds thrust
facts.source_quote: four RS-25 engines produce up to 2 million pounds of combined thrust to help launch the SLS rocket
